statement: A batch op checks the contract's batch limits when it is queued, and a full batch is a refusal, not a throw. The TS builder has no hash-ladder registration op kind yet: their limit of 32 and their place in the total of 50 are not checked there (J builder backlog).

layers.arrival: owed: spec thread, next Arrival page (id not in a name yet)

layers.contract: n/a: the check is made off-chain when the op is queued; the limits themselves are the contract's, held by J5 (the signed gas budget) and R-OOG (a cap bounds gas), tested in stress/BatchBounds.t.sol
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: R-J3 the limits are the ones DepositoryBounds and the Depository carry
R-J3 a full draft is a refusal, never a throw
R-J3 a full draft refuses with a notice and keeps what it had
R-J3 the encoded size of a group is judged when an op is queued
R-J3 the counts are judged per group, and the draft by the most one batch carries
R-J3 a group too large for one batch is refused when it is queued, so the draft can always be sealed
R-J3 a draft that could be sealed once can still be sealed after a send regroups it
R-J3 payments waiting for funding never refuse a dispute step
R-J3 every group of the draft is judged, not the first or the last
R-J3 the size limit is inclusive: exactly 256 KiB is one batch, 32 bytes more is not
R-J3 fitPrefix: the longest front of a group that is one batch
